definition: An app or spreadsheet that records money you spend (and often income) by date, category, and payment mode so you can see where cash and UPI goes.
A habit and tool for logging spends the same day they happen — cash, UPI, or cards — instead of reconstructing the week from memory.
An expense tracker you can try without a monthly subscription. Kharch Log uses a one-time lifetime unlock instead of recurring SaaS fees.
An expense tracker built for India’s Unified Payments Interface — capturing small transfers that are easy to forget after a busy day.
Software that reads bank or UPI debit/credit SMS on your phone (with permission) and turns them into ledger rows you can approve or edit.
Keeping your money book in a Google Sheet you own in Drive — often paired with a mobile app that appends rows instead of locking history in a vendor cloud.
A spreadsheet workbook (often .xlsx) used as an income and expense ledger. Powerful for pivots; weak if you never open the laptop after UPI spends.
A two-sided money book that logs money in and money out so you can compute savings rate, not only spending totals.
A view or sheet that groups spends by calendar month for rent, EMI, groceries, and category totals at month-end.
A short review cadence — usually Sunday — to catch missed UPI payments and reset categories before the next week.
A system for an individual’s cash flow: income, expenses, bills, and savings — not enterprise accounting software.
Expense tracking for one person or household ledger shared with family — categories like food, travel, rent, and UPI transfers.
A shared money book where partners or household members see the same ledger — often via a shared Google Sheet.
Tools that compare planned spend vs actuals by category. Spreadsheets and Sheets pivots work well once daily capture is reliable.
Focus on money out — cash, UPI, cards — with categories and dates so you can spot leaks like food delivery or transfers.
Tracking recurring payments (rent, EMI, utilities, subscriptions) with payees and due habits so nothing surprises you mid-month.
The durable list of dated transactions — traditionally a notebook or Excel sheet; in Kharch Log, your Google Sheet is the ledger.
Everyday spending in Indian usage — chai, auto, UPI to friends, kirana — the small amounts that vanish without a daily log.
Hindi/Urdu for expense or spending. “Kharch Log” means a log of your spends — the core idea behind the app.
Android permission that lets an app read payment alert SMS on-device. Required for bank/UPI auto-capture; unclear messages should still need your approval.
A queue for SMS-detected transactions that are unclear or incomplete — approve, reject, or edit before they become permanent ledger rows.
Adding a spend by speaking amount and details, then confirming — useful when your hands are full after a purchase.
A label such as Food, Travel, Rent, or Shopping used to group transactions for reports and monthly reviews.
How you paid — UPI, cash, card, net banking — so you can separate wallet spends from cash without mixing them in reports.
Sharing or reconciling spends across roommates or partners. A shared Google Sheet often works better than locked family-plan apps.
Tracking common home costs — groceries, help, utilities, EMI — in one ledger visible to the household.
Pay once for ongoing use of the app without a monthly subscription. Kharch Log lifetime unlock is a one-time fee on the website.
Limited OAuth access (drive.file) so an app can only use Drive files it creates for you — not your entire Drive.
A summary by day, category, or payee. On phone you get Today views; in Sheets you can pivot and chart deeper reports.
A shareable PDF of a logged expense for reimbursements or records — while the Google Sheet remains the source of truth.
Logging physical cash spends that never appear in bank SMS — still critical for honest daily kharch totals.
Recording equated monthly installments as recurring expenses so month-end totals include loans and device EMIs.
Income minus expenses over a period, as a percentage of income. Needs both sides logged in an income and expense tracker.
Using Excel or Google Sheets as your primary finance record — flexible and portable if capture stays complete.
Kharch Log is a personal daily expense tracker — not tax software. You do not need Form 16 to use it, and it does not generate Form 16 or file ITR for you.
An expense app that never asks for net banking or account credentials. Kharch Log uses optional SMS capture on your phone plus manual/voice entry instead of bank logins.
An Android expense tracker you install from a signed APK download (sideload) rather than only from Play Store — useful when the developer ships direct updates from their site.
Tracking spends across PhonePe, Google Pay, Paytm and other UPI apps in one ledger — usually via bank/UPI SMS, not by linking each wallet login.
A shared money book for PG or flatmates — often a Google Sheet plus an Android logger so rent, groceries, and UPI splits stay visible to everyone who has Sheet access.
Expense tracking without a monthly SaaS fee. Kharch Log uses a one-time ₹149 lifetime unlock instead of recurring subscriptions.
Hindi/Urdu for a simple money account or ledger — the everyday hisab of cash and UPI that Kharch Log keeps in your Google Sheet.
Logging spends on-device even when data is patchy; sync to Google Sheets when you are back online. SMS capture still needs the phone to receive messages.
